Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Its discovery estimate is near the approximate 10% absolute-mean threshold of outcome_013 (~0.027), with interval +0.0037 to +0.0502, so it is statistically nonzero under the discovery model but not interval-supported as clinically meaningful. I therefore propose comparisons that test whether the feature_027 signal is localized to an interpretable context, interacts with feature_065, extends to other dependency outcomes, or is merely a borderline or confounded result.  First, I test feature_027 on outcome_013 within feature_045=1 and feature_045=0 contexts. I anticipate uncertain directions because there is no direct evidence that feature_027 relates to feature_045. The alternatives are: clinically meaningful positive associations in both strata; attenuation in one stratum; or no clinically meaningful association in either.  Second, I register a feature_065-by-feature_027 interaction for outcome_013. H74 shows a larger positive feature_027 contrast within feature_065=1 (+0.071) than H75 does within feature_065=0 (+0.014), although H74 is imprecise and post-hoc. A positive interaction would support context-dependence of feature_027; a null interaction would favor interpreting H67 as an overall but borderline association; an opposite or very imprecise interaction would weaken the secondary signal.  Third, I test feature_065 within feature_027=0 and feature_027=1 contexts. This is the reciprocal sensitivity analysis for the main finding. Because feature_065=1 has an accepted large stronger-dependency association overall, I anticipate a raw negative contrast in both strata, i.e., positive signed estimates under direction -1. If the feature_065 association remains large when feature_027=0 and feature_027=1, the main association is less likely to be driven or confounded by feature_027. If it attenuates strongly in one stratum, that would be evidence for context-dependence or correlation rather than robust independent association.  Fourth, I screen feature_027 across other dependency outcomes in the same direction as H67: feature_027=1 associated with a less negative score. This is deliberately broad but not random: H67 provides a concrete direction, and H8 for outcome_005 was weakly positive under the same raw sign but below threshold. I prioritize outcome_006 and outcome_014 because their clinical thresholds are much smaller, about 0.0093, so a raw positive effect near 0.027 would be clinically large if it transfers. I also test outcome_015, outcome_012, outcome_008, and outcome_011 because their approximate thresholds are 0.0248-0.0301; a raw effect similar to H67 would be borderline or subthreshold in some of these outcomes. For outcome_006, outcome_014, and outcome_015 I anticipate a positive raw direction because a genuine feature_027 marker would likely transfer the same sign if it reflects a broader dependency-associated profile. For outcome_012, outcome_008, and outcome_011 I keep expectation uncertain because the effect size may be diluted or outcome-specific.  All estimates remain interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For outcome_013, outcome_015, outcome_012, outcome_008, and outcome_011 positive direction claims mean feature_027=1 is less negative, i.e., weaker dependency under the exposed-minus-comparator contrast. For outcome_006 and outcome_014 positive claims also mean feature_027=1 is less negative relative to their smaller absolute means. record.narrative:
All returned estimates are interpreted directly as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. Positive signed estimates support the stated association. For direction=-1 claims such as H79/H80, a positive signed estimate means the exposed predictor is associated with a more negative outcome_013 dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction=+1 feature_027 claims, a positive signed estimate means feature_027=1 is associated with a less negative score, i.e. weaker dependency under the stated contrast. I again used an approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold because the dependency scores are negative: about 0.0269 for outcome_013, 0.0093 for outcome_006/outcome_014, about 0.0248-0.0250 for outcome_012/outcome_015/outcome_005, about 0.0282 for outcome_008, and about 0.0301 for outcome_011.

H76 is the most decision-relevant borderline discovery: within feature_045=1, feature_027=1 versus 0 has signed mean_difference +0.0743, interval +0.0278 to +0.1207. The interval is entirely above the outcome_013 threshold, but only barely, and the claim is subgroup-specific after several feature_027 tests. This makes it scientifically promising but not robust enough to accept without validation; I keep it unresolved and active and request independent validation. H77 in the feature_045=0 complement is weak (+0.0101, interval -0.0168 to +0.0370), so it is unresolved and deferred rather than interpreted as formal evidence of context dependence. The formal feature_027-by-feature_065 interaction H78 is also unresolved/deferred: the point estimate is large (+0.0572), but the interval -0.0256 to +0.1399 includes null and subthreshold effects, so no interaction should be accepted.

For the reciprocal feature_065/outcome_013 sensitivity panel, H79 strongly supports feature_065=1 versus 0 among feature_027=0 cells: +0.1269, interval +0.0878 to +0.1660, well above the clinical threshold. I accept H79 and close it because it extends the already accepted main feature_065/outcome_013 association and shows that the main signal is not absent in the feature_027=0 complement. H80 within feature_027=1 is attenuated and imprecise (+0.0697, interval -0.0035 to +0.1430), so it remains unresolved and deferred; it raises the possibility of context dependence or reduced power, but it does not overturn the broad feature_065 association.

The cross-outcome feature_027 screen produced one exceptionally strong signal and several non-supportive results. H82 for outcome_014 shows a positive signed difference of +0.7961, interval +0.7759 to +0.8163, vastly exceeding the approximately 0.0093 clinical threshold for outcome_014. Under the Welch model and pre-specified direction, this interval supports a clinically meaningful association in which feature_027=1 is associated with a much less negative outcome_014 score. I accept H82 as a dataset-internal association and keep it active because the effect is surprisingly large and could reflect either a real subgroup-specific dependency pattern or a coding/leakage-like artifact. I prioritize validation of H76 instead of H82 because H82 is not decision-limited by sampling uncertainty under the current model, whereas H76 is near the threshold; also, validation of H82 would not by itself rule out systematic predictor-outcome construction leakage if such leakage were present. This is a limitation, not a causal or mechanistic conclusion.

The other feature_027 cross-outcome claims are not accepted. H81 outcome_006 has a signed estimate +0.0088, just below the approximate threshold but with interval -0.0325 to +0.0501 that includes clinically meaningful effects, so it is unresolved and deferred rather than rejected. H83 outcome_015, H84 outcome_012, H85 outcome_008, and H86 outcome_011 all have signed point estimates below threshold or opposite the claimed positive direction, with upper confidence bounds below the relevant clinical thresholds; therefore their claimed positive feature_027 associations are rejected as clinically unsupported in this dataset and closed.

H67 remains unresolved and active. The new evidence suggests that if the feature_027/outcome_013 reversal is real, it may be concentrated in the feature_045=1 context (H76) rather than being stable overall (H77 weak), but H67 cannot be accepted because its overall interval still includes subthreshold values and H76 is itself borderline. H74 is deferred because the new feature_045 localization and formal interaction analyses are now more informative than the earlier post-hoc feature_065 stratum. Overall, the robust core remains feature_065=1 associated with substantially more negative outcome_013 scores, now further supported in the feature_027=0 stratum. The strongest new secondary discovery is feature_027=1 associated with a much less negative outcome_014 score, but it should be treated cautiously as a dataset-internal association with potential coding or leakage concerns. No causal, mechanistic, or external generalization is inferred.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative:
All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. A positive signed estimate supports the stated association. For feature_065 claims with direction -1, positive means feature_065=1 is associated with a more negative CRISPR dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. Approximate 10%-absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0269 for outcome_013, 0.0250 for outcome_015, and 0.0260 for outcome_002.

H58 is the formal claim that feature_045=1 strengthens the feature_065 association with a more negative outcome_013 score. Discovery R58 gave +0.0669, interval -0.0175 to +0.1514, so it excluded neither null nor clinically subthreshold modification and its lower bound was below the threshold. Independent validation R102 was opposite in signed direction, -0.0356, interval -0.1497 to +0.0786, again crossing null and not clinically interval-supported. The discovery and independent validation are inconsistent, and neither provides interval-level evidence above the threshold. I therefore reject H58 and close it as not evidence-supported in this dataset. This does not prove absence of interaction; it means the data do not support a clinically meaningful feature_045 modification of the main feature_065/outcome_013 association. Because direct accepted estimates exist within both feature_045=1 and feature_045=0 strata, the more parsimonious dataset-internal conclusion is that feature_065 is associated with lower outcome_013 scores in both contexts rather than being reliably modified by feature_045.

H69 is validated independently. Discovery was +0.1278, interval +0.0775 to +0.1781, and validation R103 is +0.0998, interval +0.0331 to +0.1666. The validation lower bound exceeds the outcome_013 clinical threshold, so independent evidence supports the claim that feature_065=1 versus 0 is associated with a substantially more negative outcome_013 score within the feature_034=0 context. I keep H69 accepted and closed.

H70 is now due for its validation response. It claimed feature_065=1 versus 0 is associated with a more negative outcome_015 score within feature_045=0. Discovery was +0.0254, interval +0.0032 to +0.0476, but the lower bound did not clear the outcome_015 threshold. Validation R76 is +0.0165, interval -0.0160 to +0.0491. The validation point is below the 10% threshold and the interval includes both null and clinically subthreshold effects. I reject H70 and close it. This is a negative finding for a clinically meaningful feature_065 association with outcome_015 in that context, not proof that feature_065 has no relation to outcome_015 anywhere.

H16 is also due for its validation response. It claimed feature_065=1 versus 0 is associated with a more negative outcome_002 score among cells with high feature_043. Discovery was +0.0100, interval -0.0236 to +0.0436. Validation R77 is +0.0240, interval -0.0382 to +0.0861. Although the validation point is close to the outcome_002 threshold of about 0.0260, it does not clear it and the interval includes null and clinically subthreshold effects. I reject H16 and close it. The data do not support this outcome_002 association as clinically meaningful.

The current evidence base remains strongest for feature_065=1 being associated with a much more negative outcome_013 dependency score, with independent validation for the feature_034=0 stratum and accepted context-specific estimates across feature_043 strata, feature_045=1, feature_045=0, and feature_027=0. The secondary feature_045 modification pathway is now closed without evidence support. record.narrative:
No assessments are due, so this stage registers follow-up hypotheses. All future estimates should be interpreted as already signed to the registered direction: for feature_027/outcome_014 claims with direction +1, a positive signed estimate means feature_027=1 is associated with a less negative dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency; for feature_065/outcome_013 and outcome_015 claims with direction -1, a positive signed estimate means feature_065=1 is associated with a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. Approximate 10%-absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0093 for outcome_014, 0.0269 for outcome_013, and 0.0250 for outcome_015.

The accepted feature_027/outcome_014 association is exceptionally large and remains active. H99 and H100 already test direct feature_043 contexts. I now refine H82 in two additional broad predictor contexts: feature_034=1/0 and feature_054 level_002/level_001. These are useful because feature_034 and feature_054 are nontrivial categorical predictors that were not the primary drivers of the feature_027/outcome_014 pattern in earlier interaction tests. If these strata are also interval-supported far above threshold, it would strengthen the conclusion that the association is broad within this dataset rather than confined to one tested context, though it would not distinguish a genuine biological association from a coding or leakage-like dataset-internal structure. If any stratum is absent, subthreshold, or highly imprecise, that would support context dependence and would warrant a more cautious, context-specific conclusion rather than treating H82 as a general dataset-wide marker association.

I also refine the primary feature_065/outcome_013 association within feature_054 level_002 and level_001. The earlier interaction H64 suggested no clinically meaningful modification by feature_054 but was imprecise. Direct stratum estimates can clarify whether feature_065 remains robust in both feature_054 contexts or whether one context is attenuated. Since the broad feature_065/outcome_013 finding is already supported across several contexts, these tests are mainly for precision and context confirmation. Acceptance would require the signed interval to exclude both null and subthreshold effects; a point estimate above threshold with a wide interval including null should remain unresolved.

Finally, I register two broad screens of feature_042, an untested binary marker with about 23% prevalence. For outcome_013, I test the hypothesis that feature_042=1 is associated with a more negative dependency score, parallel in direction to the robust feature_065 association but not expected a priori to have the same magnitude. For outcome_014, I test whether feature_042=1 is associated with a less negative score, in the same direction as the exceptional feature_027 effect. These are exploratory: acceptance would identify another clinically interval-supported marker on an important outcome, while null or subthreshold results would close a common marker pathway and reinforce that feature_065/outcome_013 and feature_027/outcome_014 are the main dataset-internal signals. I also follow up the borderline unrestricted feature_065/outcome_015 finding by testing the low feature_043 stratum. If the lower interval bound clears the outcome_015 threshold there, this would refine the cross-outcome signal to a specific context; if not, it strengthens the conclusion that feature_065 is primarily associated with outcome_013 rather than clinically meaningful outcome_015 differences. All proposals are dataset-internal association tests only; acceptance or nonacceptance does not establish causality, mechanism, or external generalizability.

record.narrative:
All newly delivered estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For feature_027/outcome_014 claims with direction +1, a positive estimate means feature_027=1 is associated with a less negative CRISPR dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency; for feature_065/outcome_013 and feature_065/outcome_015 claims with direction -1, a positive estimate means feature_065=1 is associated with a more negative score, i.e. stronger dependency. I used approximate 10%-absolute-mean clinical thresholds: about 0.0093 for outcome_014, 0.0269 for outcome_013, and 0.0250 for outcome_015.

H99 and H100 test feature_027/outcome_014 in high and lower feature_043 contexts. Both are enormous and precise: +0.8007, interval +0.7580 to +0.8433, and +0.7947, interval +0.7717 to +0.8177. Their lower bounds are far above both null and the outcome_014 threshold. I accept and close both direct strata. H102 and H103 test feature_034 contexts, and H104 and H105 test feature_054 levels; all four are similarly interval-supported: +0.7886/+0.8042 in feature_034=1/0 and +0.8049/+0.7929 in feature_054 level_002/level_001, with lower bounds near +0.76 to +0.78. Together with earlier accepted feature_065 and feature_045 strata, this means the accepted overall feature_027/outcome_014 association is not confined to any one tested predictor context. This strongly supports that the association is broad within this supplied dataset, but the effect is so large that it remains prudent to suspect a dataset-internal coding or leakage-like structure rather than a generalizable biological relationship. I therefore request independent validation of H82, the original unrestricted feature_027/outcome_014 association, to test split stability. Validation cannot exclude a leakage-like dataset structure, but failure would be highly informative.

H106 and H107 directly estimate feature_065/outcome_013 within feature_054 level_002 and level_001. They are +0.1242, interval +0.0575 to +0.1909, and +0.1144, interval +0.0736 to +0.1552. Both lower bounds exceed the outcome_013 threshold and zero. I accept and close both. This refines the earlier imprecise feature_054 interaction by showing that feature_065 remains associated with much stronger outcome_013 dependency in both feature_054 contexts, reinforcing the primary finding.

H101 is the reciprocal feature_045/outcome_013 contrast within feature_065=0. The signed estimate is only +0.0072, interval -0.0129 to +0.0274. Its point estimate is far below the clinical threshold, and the interval does not provide interval-level support; it barely retains enough upper-bound uncertainty to prevent a clean rejection of a marginal positive effect. I leave it unresolved but close investigation because the formal feature_045 modification claim H58 has already failed validation and the direct feature_045 strata of feature_065/outcome_013 are already accepted, making this reciprocal contrast low priority.

H108 tests feature_042 as a potential new marker for outcome_013 with hypothesized more negative scores. The signed estimate is -0.0016, interval -0.0244 to +0.0213. It is essentially null, and the upper bound is below the outcome_013 threshold, so the interval excludes a clinically meaningful positive association in the registered direction. I reject and close. H109 tests feature_042 as a potential weaker-dependency marker for outcome_014 with hypothesized less negative scores. The signed estimate is -0.0351, interval -0.0714 to +0.0012. The upper bound is below the outcome_014 threshold, excluding a clinically meaningful positive effect in the registered direction. I reject and close. These results indicate that feature_042 does not add a new clinically meaningful signal on either main outcome.

H110 tests feature_065/outcome_015 in low feature_043. The signed estimate is +0.0273, interval -0.0095 to +0.0641. It is borderline in point estimate relative to the outcome_015 threshold but is not interval-supported, because the interval includes null and subthreshold effects. I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than closing the cross-outcome signal entirely; however, given prior borderline and failed validation results for feature_065/outcome_015, it is not a priority. No causal, mechanistic, or external generalization is inferred from any of these dataset-internal associations.

record.narrative:
All estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For feature_027/outcome_014 claims with direction +1, positive signed values mean feature_027=1 is associated with a less negative CRISPR dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency. For feature_065/outcome_013 claims with direction -1, positive signed values mean feature_065=1 is associated with a more negative score, i.e. stronger dependency. I continue to use the run's approximate 10%-absolute-mean clinical thresholds, about 0.0269 for outcome_013 and about 0.0093 for outcome_014.

H82 is the unrestricted feature_027=1 versus 0 association with outcome_014. Discovery R84 was +0.7961, 95% interval +0.7759 to +0.8163. Independent validation R116 is +0.8005, independent interval +0.7721 to +0.8290. The validation point estimate is almost identical to discovery, and its lower bound is enormous and far above both the null and the outcome_014 clinical threshold. I therefore accept H82 and close it. The feature_027/outcome_014 association is not merely split-stable at the unrestricted level; it is also direct in previously accepted strata defined by feature_065, feature_045, feature_043, feature_034, and feature_054. The evidence strongly supports that, within this supplied dataset, feature_027=1 is associated with dramatically weaker outcome_014 dependency. Because the effect is implausibly large relative to other marker effects, the appropriate conclusion is a robust dataset-internal association, not a causal or generalizable biological dependency relationship. This also leaves open the possibility that feature_027 behaves like a coding or leakage-like marker for outcome_014 in the constructed dataset.

H76 is the feature_027=1 versus 0 association with outcome_013 within feature_045=1. Discovery R78 was +0.0743, 95% interval +0.0278 to +0.1207, which was just above the outcome_013 threshold at its lower bound. Independent validation R89 was +0.0179, independent interval -0.0475 to +0.0833. The validation point estimate is below the clinical threshold and the interval includes null and clinically subthreshold effects. The two splits are therefore inconsistent in the clinically relevant range, and the independent evidence does not support a stable clinically meaningful association. I keep H76 rejected and closed. This is a negative finding for the feature_045=1 subgroup: feature_027 is not shown here to have a robust clinically meaningful association with outcome_013 in that context. It does not prove that no such association exists elsewhere, but the supplied discovery and validation data do not support it.

The current evidence base is now clearest around two dataset-internal findings. First, feature_065=1 is associated with much stronger outcome_013 dependency, with interval-supported estimates across broad and multiple context-specific analyses and with independent validation in the feature_034=0 stratum. Second, feature_027=1 is associated with much weaker outcome_014 dependency overall, with independent validation and consistent context-specific direct estimates. Secondary pathways are not supported as clinically meaningful associations: feature_045 modification of the feature_065/outcome_013 association was not supported after failed validation; feature_042 was not supported for outcome_013 or outcome_014; and feature_065/outcome_015 and feature_065/outcome_002 contexts were not clinically interval-supported after validation. The main unresolved items are borderline or low-priority cross-outcome contrasts such as feature_065/outcome_015, feature_027/outcome_013 overall, and some interactions, but these do not alter the primary supported conclusions.

If further investigation were warranted, the most informative next steps would not be more validation of the already stable H82 or H69 findings. Instead, effort would be better used to screen remaining untested predictors on the key outcomes, or to examine whether feature_027/outcome_014 reflects a dataset-internal coding or surrogate-variable structure. For the present synthesis, the scientifically supported conclusions are association-only and dataset-internal: feature_065 is robustly associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency, and feature_027 is robustly associated with weaker outcome_014 dependency.

Study instructions:

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due. These new proposals are interpreted with the current sign convention: for direction -1 outcomes, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 outcomes, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative score, i.e. weaker dependency. Approximate 10%-absolute-mean thresholds are about 0.0269 for outcome_013, 0.0093 for outcome_014, 0.0415 for outcome_001, and 0.0256 for outcome_016.

The two dominant dataset-internal findings are feature_065=1 associated with much stronger outcome_013 dependency and feature_027=1 associated with much weaker outcome_014 dependency. Rather than repeatedly validating those already stable claims, I now ask whether they hold in clinically interpretable contexts and whether feature_057, the available numeric feature whose distribution is compatible with a progression-free-survival-like severity variable, is itself associated with dependency scores or marks contexts where the primary marker effects persist. I test the primary feature_065/outcome_013 and feature_027/outcome_014 associations in the upper clinical context feature_057=10 and in a lower clinical context feature_057<=5. For feature_065, the anticipated raw contrast is negative, because higher feature_065 prevalence is expected to correspond to stronger outcome_013 dependency; after direction -1 this would appear as a positive signed estimate. For feature_027, the anticipated raw contrast is positive, because feature_027=1 has been associated with weaker outcome_014 dependency. If these intervals exclude both null and the relevant clinical thresholds, this would broaden the accepted findings into clinically meaningful contexts. If an interval is null or subthreshold, that would indicate that the previously accepted overall association does not persist uniformly in that specific clinical context.

I also directly test feature_057 high value 10 versus low value 5 for outcome_014 and outcome_013. This is a falsifiable high-versus-low severity contrast: high feature_057 is hypothesized to associate with less negative dependency scores, i.e. weaker dependency, so the claim direction is +1 and the anticipated raw contrast is positive. This contrast may be less precise if the exact 5-value cell is sparse; if it does not meet the 20-observation cell requirement, it will not produce eligible evidence, and the context tests above remain useful. Direct evidence of an interval-supported association between high feature_057 and weaker dependency on either primary outcome would be a new clinically interpretable dataset-internal finding; null or subthreshold evidence would suggest that feature_057 is not strongly associated with these dependency scores in this dataset.

Finally, I add screens of previously untested binary markers. Feature_032 is rare but has enough expected cells, and feature_022 is uncommon and has robust cells. For outcome_013, the hypothesis direction is -1: if positive signed estimates exceed threshold, these markers are associated with stronger dependency. For outcome_014, the direction is +1: positive signed estimates would indicate weaker dependency, analogous to feature_027. These are exploratory: acceptance would identify additional clinically meaningful markers; rejection or unresolved low-magnitude results would strengthen the conclusion that feature_065/outcome_013 and feature_027/outcome_014 are the primary marker signals. I also test whether the exceptional feature_027 signal is specific to outcome_014 or has cross-outcome associations with outcome_001 and outcome_016. A positive signed estimate above threshold would support a broader weak-dependency association; a null or subthreshold result would increase confidence that feature_027's huge effect is largely outcome_014-specific within this dataset. All interpretations remain dataset-internal association statements only, without causal, mechanistic, or external generalization claims.

record.narrative: All newly delivered estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For feature_065/outcome_013 claims with direction -1, a positive signed estimate means feature_065=1 is associated with a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. For feature_027/outcome_014 and feature_057/outcome_014 claims with direction +1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency. I used the same approximate 10%-absolute-mean clinical thresholds as before: about 0.0269 for outcome_013, 0.0093 for outcome_014, 0.0415 for outcome_001, and 0.0256 for outcome_016. H113 and H114 directly test the primary feature_065/outcome_013 association in feature_057=10 and feature_057<=5 contexts. They are +0.1138, interval +0.0704 to +0.1572, and +0.1220, interval +0.0640 to +0.1800. Both lower bounds are far above zero and above the outcome_013 clinical threshold, so I accept and close both. H115 and H116 directly test the primary feature_027/outcome_014 association in the same feature_057 contexts. They are +0.8139, interval +0.7880 to +0.8398, and +0.7705, interval +0.7384 to +0.8026. Both lower bounds are enormous relative to the outcome_014 threshold, so I accept and close both. These context results strengthen the robustness of the two main dataset-internal marker associations, but they do not establish causality or external generalizability. H111 directly tests feature_057 value 10 versus 5 for outcome_014 with hypothesized weaker dependency. The signed estimate is -0.0055, interval -0.0444 to +0.0333. It provides no support for a clinically meaningful positive weaker-dependency effect, but the upper bound exceeds the outcome_014 threshold, so the interval does not exclude a clinically meaningful effect in the claimed direction. I leave it unresolved and deferred. H112 directly tests feature_057 value 10 versus 5 for outcome_013 with hypothesized weaker dependency. The signed estimate is -0.0060, interval -0.0294 to +0.0173. The upper bound is below the outcome_013 clinical threshold, so a clinically meaningful positive weaker-dependency effect is excluded in the registered direction. I reject and close. H117 tests feature_032 on outcome_013 with hypothesized stronger dependency. The signed estimate is -0.0045, interval -0.0510 to +0.0421. This is essentially null, but the upper bound exceeds the outcome_013 threshold, so a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency effect is not excluded. I leave it unresolved and deferred, primarily because the marker is rare and imprecise. H118 tests feature_032 on outcome_014 with hypothesized weaker dependency. The signed estimate is -0.0685, interval -0.1381 to +0.0012. The upper bound is below the outcome_014 threshold, excluding a clinically meaningful positive weaker-dependency effect. I reject and close. H119 and H120 test feature_022 on outcome_013 and outcome_014. Both are close to null: outcome_013 -0.0034, interval -0.0349 to +0.0282; outcome_014 -0.0014, interval -0.0499 to +0.0471. Each interval includes zero and clinically meaningful positive effects in the registered direction, so neither can be accepted or cleanly rejected; I leave them unresolved and deferred. H121 tests feature_027 on outcome_001 with hypothesized weaker dependency. The signed estimate is +0.0059, interval -0.0345 to +0.0463. The interval includes zero and clinically meaningful positive effects near the outcome_001 threshold, but the point estimate is far below threshold. I leave it unresolved and deferred. H122 tests feature_027 on outcome_016 with hypothesized weaker dependency. The signed estimate is +0.0044, interval -0.0157 to +0.0244. The upper bound is below the approximate outcome_016 threshold of 0.0256, so a clinically meaningful weaker-dependency association is excluded in the registered direction. I reject and close. I did not request independent validation: the new accepted claims H113-H116 are context-specific extensions of already independently validated primary associations for feature_065/outcome_013 and feature_027/outcome_014, and the newly null or borderline screens are not high-priority claims whose validation would change the main conclusions. The feature_027/outcome_014 association remains suspiciously large, so interpretation should remain dataset-internal and association-only, with leakage-like or coding-like structure still possible.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum

record.narrative:
I reassess the two validation response deadlines using the current sign convention. For feature_065/outcome_013 claims with direction -1, positive signed estimates mean feature_065=1 is associated with a more negative CRISPR dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. For feature_027/outcome_014 claims with direction +1, positive signed estimates mean feature_027=1 is associated with a less negative score, i.e. weaker dependency. I continue to treat effects around the run's approximate 10%-absolute-mean threshold, about 0.0269 for outcome_013 and 0.0093 for outcome_014, as clinically meaningful.  
H69 tests feature_065=1 versus 0 for outcome_013 in the feature_034=0 stratum. Discovery R69 gave signed +0.1278, 95% interval +0.0775 to +0.1781. Independent validation R103 gave signed +0.0998, independent interval +0.0331 to +0.1666. Both intervals exclude zero and have lower bounds above the outcome_013 clinical threshold, and the validation point estimate is slightly smaller but still large. I therefore accept H69 and close it. This independently supports, in a clinically relevant feature_034 stratum, that feature_065 is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency within this dataset. Together with the earlier accepted overall H29, accepted feature_043-high H13/H28, accepted feature_034=1 H68, accepted feature_045 strata H60/H65, accepted feature_027=0 H79, accepted feature_054 strata H106/H107, and accepted feature_057-context H113/H114, the evidence supports a broad and robust dataset-internal mean_difference association, not a causal biological effect or external generalization.  
H58 tests whether the feature_065 effect on outcome_013 is modified by feature_045=1. The registered positive signed direction corresponds to a stronger feature_065 dependency difference in feature_045=1 than in its complement. Discovery R58 gave +0.0669, interval -0.0175 to +0.1514, which does not provide interval-level support. Validation R102 gave the opposite signed estimate, -0.0356, independent interval -0.1497 to +0.0786. The two independent estimates are inconsistent in sign, and neither supplies interval-level evidence for a clinically meaningful positive interaction. I keep H58 rejected and closed. This is a negative finding for feature_045 effect modification: the available data do not support a clinically meaningful interaction of this kind, even though the interval-level null is not perfectly sharp because the validation interval remains wide.  
Overall supported findings. The strongest supported conclusion is that feature_065=1 is robustly associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency across many eligibility and subgroup contexts. The magnitude is consistently around +0.10 to +0.17 signed, and the validated strata H13 and H69 both have independent intervals with lower bounds above the clinical threshold. The pattern is most consistent with a marker-like association: feature_065 identifies a subgroup with more negative outcome_013 dependency scores. The second supported conclusion is that feature_027=1 is robustly associated with dramatically weaker outcome_014 dependency. The overall discovery estimate was +0.7961, interval +0.7759 to +0.8163, and validation H82 gave +0.8005, interval +0.7721 to +0.8290. This effect is orders of magnitude larger than ordinary marker effects and is reproduced in almost every examined stratum, including feature_065, feature_045, feature_043, feature_034, feature_054, and feature_057 contexts. I therefore accept it as a robust dataset-internal association only. Its size is biologically implausible as a simple dependency association and is compatible with a surrogate, coding-like, or leakage-like structure in this supplied dataset.  
Negative findings. The data do not support feature_045 modification of the feature_065/outcome_013 mean difference after validation (H58), and several other feature_065 interactions are rejected, including feature_034 (H52), feature_043 median/high interactions (H39/H27), and feature_065/outcome_002/004/006/016 associations after discovery or validation. The feature_027 association with outcome_013 within feature_045=1 (H76) failed validation and remains a negative subgroup finding. The feature_065 association with outcome_015 within feature_045=0 (H70) failed validation, supporting outcome specificity for outcome_013 rather than a broad shift across all outcomes. Many screened predictors and markers, including feature_032 for outcome_014, feature_042, feature_045 main effects in outcome_006/014 contexts, and most tested predictors outside the two core signals, do not show clinically meaningful interval-supported associations.  
Unresolved uncertainty. A few secondary contrasts remain uncertain because intervals include both null and clinically meaningful effects, though none alter the main conclusions. These include feature_057 value 10 versus 5 for outcome_014 (H111), whose upper bound exceeds the outcome_014 threshold but whose point estimate is near zero; feature_027/outcome_001 (H121); feature_022 and feature_032 for outcome_013; feature_065 for outcome_014 overall and in feature_027 strata; and several feature_027/feature_065 interactions (H78/H87/H89). These are low priority relative to the accepted core associations, and validating all of them would spend remaining validation budget without changing the primary scientific picture.  
Next analysis. The most informative next work would not be additional validation of H82 or H69, because those are already independently supported. It should focus on specificity and possible artifact structure. First, resolve the feature_065-by-feature_027 interaction for outcome_013 using the already registered H78 or related follow-up, because the feature_065 mean difference is strong in feature_027=0 but less precise in feature_027=1. Second, examine whether the huge feature_027/outcome_014 association is outcome-specific by testing feature_027 effects on the remaining outcomes in feature_065=0 or in the largest stable strata. Third, screen the remaining high-prevalence binary predictors that have not yet been tested against outcome_013 and outcome_014, because broad exploration can still identify additional markers, while low-prevalence borderline screens are less likely to change the conclusions. Throughout, all statements must remain dataset-internal associations, not causal claims, mechanistic claims, or claims of generalizability beyond this supplied dataset.

record.narrative:
These proposals are interpreted using the existing sign convention. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group has a less negative dependency score than the comparator, i.e. weaker dependency. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score than the comparator, i.e. stronger dependency. Approximate 10%-absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0249 for outcome_005, 0.0415 for outcome_001, 0.0093 for outcome_006, 0.0093 for outcome_014, 0.0269 for outcome_013, and 0.0301 for outcome_011. The goal is not to revalidate the two already dominant dataset-internal associations, but to test their specificity, possible independence structure, dose-response or severity gradients, and whether additional high-prevalence markers exist.

First, I test whether feature_027 has broader weak-dependency associations beyond outcome_014, especially in the larger feature_065=0 context. Feature_027=1 is robustly associated with dramatically weaker outcome_014 dependency, but most other feature_027-outcome tests either rejected meaningful effects in the registered direction or were unresolved. Outcome_005 previously only tested the opposite direction, so the new outcome_005 feature_027=1 versus 0 claim tests whether the observed raw tendency toward weaker dependency is clinically meaningful. Outcome_001 and outcome_006 were unresolved overall; restricting to feature_065=0 checks whether these unresolved signals are diluted by the feature_065-exposed subgroup or persist in the more stable majority context. For these direction +1 claims, acceptance would require interval support above zero and above the relevant 10% threshold for weaker dependency. Rejection or persistent imprecision would strengthen the conclusion that the enormous feature_027 signal is highly outcome_014-specific, or at least not broadly replicable across dependency scores.

Second, I address the unresolved feature_065-by-feature_027 structure for outcome_013. The strong overall and many context-specific feature_065/outcome_013 associations are supported, but the feature_065 mean difference among feature_027=1 participants is imprecise and less clearly above threshold. Rather than another broad interaction, I request a focused mean_difference of feature_065=1 versus 0 for outcome_013 among feature_027=1 participants who also have feature_045=0. This is expected to retain enough cells while removing feature_045=1 heterogeneity. If the lower bound exceeds zero and the outcome_013 threshold, this would show that the feature_065 marker association persists even in the feature_027=1 context. If it is null or subthreshold, this would suggest the feature_065 association is attenuated or conditional in that context, though it would not prove causality or mechanism.

Third, I test feature_045 for an outcome_013 association independent of feature_065. Feature_065 effects are accepted within both feature_045=0 and feature_045=1, but the main effect of feature_045 in the feature_065=0 population has not been cleanly isolated. With direction -1, a positive signed estimate means feature_045=1 is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency among feature_065=0 participants. If accepted, this would identify a second marker or correlated marker context for outcome_013. If rejected or subthreshold, it supports feature_065 specificity rather than broad marker overlap.

Fourth, I test a dose-response or severity gradient using feature_057. The prior high-versus-moderate feature_057 contrast was null for outcome_013 and imprecise for outcome_014. I now compare moderate value 5 versus low value 2 for both primary outcomes. Direction +1 and anticipated positive mean that moderate feature_057 is expected to associate with less negative scores than low feature_057, consistent with a severity gradient where higher feature_057 corresponds to weaker dependency. This is falsifiable: a monotonic gradient would show clinically meaningful positive signed effects, while null or reversed effects would argue against a simple severity-driven dependency gradient in these outcomes.

Fifth, I add broad screens of high-prevalence binary predictors that have not yet been tested against outcome_013 and outcome_014. I test feature_008=0 versus feature_008=1 and feature_030=0 versus feature_030=1. Because the positive labels are majority levels, exposed=0 deliberately tests the minority contrast. For outcome_013 direction -1, positive signed estimates mean the feature_008=0 or feature_030=0 group has stronger dependency; for outcome_014 direction +1, positive signed estimates mean those minority groups have weaker dependency. These are exploratory marker screens. Acceptance would identify additional clinically meaningful binary markers; rejection or subthreshold imprecision would further narrow the predictor landscape around the already supported feature_065/outcome_013 and feature_027/outcome_014 associations. All statements remain dataset-internal associations and do not establish causality, biological mechanism, or external generalizability.

The goal is not to revalidate the two already dominant dataset-internal associations, but to test their specificity, possible independence structure, dose-response or severity gradients, and whether additional high-prevalence markers exist.\n\nFirst, I test whether feature_027 has broader weak-dependency associations beyond outcome_014, especially in the larger feature_065=0 context. Feature_027=1 is robustly associated with dramatically weaker outcome_014 dependency, but most other feature_027-outcome tests either rejected meaningful effects in the registered direction or were unresolved. Outcome_005 previously only tested the opposite direction, so the new outcome_005 feature_027=1 versus 0 claim tests whether the observed raw tendency toward weaker dependency is clinically meaningful. Outcome_001 and outcome_006 were unresolved overall; restricting to feature_065=0 checks whether these unresolved signals are diluted by the feature_065-exposed subgroup or persist in the more stable majority context. For these direction +1 claims, acceptance would require interval support above zero and above the relevant 10% threshold for weaker dependency. Rejection or persistent imprecision would strengthen the conclusion that the enormous feature_027 signal is highly outcome_014-specific, or at least not broadly replicable across dependency scores.\n\nSecond, I address the unresolved feature_065-by-feature_027 structure for outcome_013. The strong overall and many context-specific feature_065/outcome_013 associations are supported, but the feature_065 mean difference among feature_027=1 participants is imprecise and less clearly above threshold. Rather than another broad interaction, I request a focused mean_difference of feature_065=1 versus 0 for outcome_013 among feature_027=1 participants who also have feature_045=0. This is expected to retain enough cells while removing feature_045=1 heterogeneity. If the lower bound exceeds zero and the outcome_013 threshold, this would show that the feature_065 marker association persists even in the feature_027=1 context. If it is null or subthreshold, this would suggest the feature_065 association is attenuated or conditional in that context, though it would not prove causality or mechanism.\n\nThird, I test feature_045 for an outcome_013 association independent of feature_065. Feature_065 effects are accepted within both feature_045=0 and feature_045=1, but the main effect of feature_045 in the feature_065=0 population has not been cleanly isolated. With direction -1, a positive signed estimate means feature_045=1 is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency among feature_065=0 participants. If accepted, this would identify a second marker or correlated marker context for outcome_013. If rejected or subthreshold, it supports feature_065 specificity rather than broad marker overlap.\n\nFourth, I test a dose-response or severity gradient using feature_057. The prior high-versus-moderate feature_057 contrast was null for outcome_013 and imprecise for outcome_014. I now compare moderate value 5 versus low value 2 for both primary outcomes. Direction +1 and anticipated positive mean that moderate feature_057 is expected to associate with less negative scores than low feature_057, consistent with a severity gradient where higher feature_057 corresponds to weaker dependency. This is falsifiable: a monotonic gradient would show clinically meaningful positive signed effects, while null or reversed effects would argue against a simple severity-driven dependency gradient in these outcomes.\n\nFifth, I add broad screens of high-prevalence binary predictors that have not yet been tested against outcome_013 and outcome_014. For outcome_013 direction -1, positive signed estimates mean the feature_008=0 or feature_030=0 group has stronger dependency; for outcome_014 direction +1, positive signed estimates mean those minority groups have weaker dependency. These are exploratory marker screens. Acceptance would identify additional clinically meaningful binary markers; rejection or subthreshold imprecision would further narrow the predictor landscape around the already supported feature_065/outcome_013 and feature_027/outcome_014 associations. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.
